newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products knocked lower by crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products knocked lower by crude.

text.p: Med oil products were weaker on Friday, largely because of easier crude, traders said.
Gasoline was weaker in line with futures. The region remains tight, and prices are likely to find support from potential buying across the Atlantic as well as from further east.
Naphtha was easier by $5 a tonne or so in line with weaker crude. Several traders said prices could start heading down to the $200 mark for cif cargoes from their current $208 level.
High sulphur fuel oil was notionally weaker as northwest European prices fell sharply, traders said. No Isab barrels were heard available in the prompt period.
It was seen hard to pin down prices, given the differing qualities of material under discussion.

Low sulphur fuel oil was weaker in line with crude. Traders saw only a little buying interest - one for 25,000 tonnes of product for early March, and another for southern France, but avails, especially in northwest Europe, were seen more than adequate to cover it.

Gas oil premiums were a touch stronger, but a sharp drop on IPE futures shaved manged to pull prices lower. Traders said Russian material had gained to high cif flat quotes high cif from yesterday's high cif quotes -50 cents.
Italian spec was at high fob quotes -$1.
Interest remained to take material to South America, but local demand was largely absent.
